analysis.one_liner: ICICI Bank is India's second-largest private sector bank, taking deposits and lending across retail, SME, corporate and rural segments, with insurance and asset-management subsidiaries alongside.
analysis.whats_happening: ICICI Bank's board meets on 17 October 2026 (three days from now) to approve Q2 FY27 (July-September 2026) results, with an earnings call the same day. In the preceding quarter (Q1 FY27, April-June 2026), standalone net profit rose 15.9% year-on-year to ₹14,804 crore and net interest income grew 12.7% to ₹24,384 crore, with loan growth of 19.6%. Separately, the bank has disclosed GST demand notices of about ₹229 crore and ₹16.76 crore in recent months, which are contingent liabilities rather than confirmed losses.
analysis.plain_terms: This is one of the two private banks that effectively set the pace for Indian banking, and it's been taking market share while growing loans by roughly a fifth a year. The tension is that the market already knows this and prices it in: the stock has nearly doubled over five years and trades at a premium to the sector, so good results are partly already paid for. The thing to watch isn't whether the bank is well run - the numbers say it is - it's whether growth this fast can continue without asset quality or margins slipping.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026): standalone PAT ₹14,804 crore, up 15.9% YoY from ₹12,768 crore; NII ₹24,384 crore, up 12.7%; NIM 4.36% (vs 4.34% a year ago and 4.32% in Q4 FY26) - broadly stable, not expanding or contracting materially. Gross NPA improved to 1.38% from 1.67% a year ago and 1.40% the previous quarter. Net NPA ticked up slightly to 0.35% from 0.33% in Q4 FY26, though still well below the 0.41% of a year ago. Provision coverage stood at 74.7%. Advances grew 19.6% YoY, led by rural/gold loans (+35.4%) and business banking (+28.2%), with retail slower at +12%. Management (Sandeep Bakhshi) said it expects loan growth to stay in the 'high teens' for the year. Q2 FY27 numbers are due 17 October 2026 and are not yet known - nothing here should be read as this quarter's result.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is up 99% over 5 years and 46.5% over 3 years, comfortably ahead of the Nifty (25% and 15% respectively) and far ahead of its peer HDFC Bank, which is down 6.9% over 5 years and 25.7% over the last year. Both 2014 and 2017 corporate actions (a 5-for-1 split and a bonus issue) are already reflected in these return figures, so there is no hidden crash to adjust for - the recent 7.1% pullback from the July 2025 peak of ₹1,464.85 to the current ₹1,360.20 looks like a normal drawdown within a strong uptrend, not a structural problem. HDFC Bank's weak showing over the same period is widely linked to its 2023 merger with its parent HDFC Ltd diluting return ratios - worth keeping in mind before reading ICICI's outperformance purely as a sign of superior execution.
analysis.valuation_read: ICICI Bank trades around 17x trailing earnings and roughly 2.5x book value, against a Financial Services sector median P/E near 15.5x - a modest premium. It is cheap relative to its own history: the current P/B is below its 10-year median of about 2.85x even though the stock sits only 7% off its all-time high. Why it carries a premium at all: consistently improving asset quality, stable margins and an ROE near 16-17%, which is high for a bank of this size. Whether that premium is justified is a judgment call the reader has to make, not a fact the numbers settle.
analysis.growth_read: This is volume-led growth, not a margin story: advances grew ~20% YoY across retail, rural, business banking and corporate segments, while NIM stayed essentially flat (4.32-4.36% over the last three quarters). That combination - book growing, margin holding rather than expanding - is a more durable form of growth than margin-led expansion on a flat loan book.
analysis.health_read: Profits are backed by a clean balance sheet: gross NPA of 1.38% and net NPA of 0.35% are low by Indian banking standards, and provision coverage of 74.7% gives a cushion against future slippage. Capital adequacy of 16.84% (CET-1 16.19%) is comfortably above the regulatory minimum of 11.70%, so there is no capital-raise overhang. The real variable here is business risk - whether rapid loan growth across rural/gold and business banking segments eventually shows up as stress - rather than financial or balance-sheet risk, which currently looks well managed.
analysis.ownership_read: ICICI Bank has no promoter group - it emerged from a 2002 merger structure and is widely held, so the usual pledging question does not apply (0% promoter, 0% pledged). As of June 2026, DIIs held about 42.3% and FIIs about 33.8%, with the remaining ~23.7% public. This is an institutionally-owned stock; there is no marquee individual investor on the register, which is typical for a company of this size and float rather than a red flag.
strengths: Advances grew 19.6% YoY in Q1 FY27, with rural/gold loans up 35.4% and business banking up 28.2%
Net interest margin held at 4.36%, essentially flat for three straight quarters despite rate moves
Gross NPA fell to 1.38% from 1.67% a year earlier, with provision coverage of 74.7%
Capital adequacy of 16.84% (CET-1 16.19%) sits well above the regulatory floor, leaving headroom to keep growing the loan book without raising capital
watchpoints: Net NPA ticked up to 0.35% from 0.33% quarter-on-quarter - small, but worth watching for a reversal of the improving trend
GST demand notices of roughly ₹229 crore and ₹16.76 crore are open contingent liabilities, not yet resolved
Stock trades at a premium to the sector median P/E (~17x vs ~15.5x), which leaves less room for a soft quarter to be shrugged off
Q2 FY27 results land on 17 October 2026, just three days out - any sign of NIM compression or loan-growth deceleration there would be the first real test of the current narrative
analysis.one_thing: The 17 October 2026 Q2 FY27 results: specifically whether NIM holds near 4.3-4.4% and whether the small quarter-on-quarter uptick in net NPA (0.33% to 0.35%) continues or reverses.
analysis.data_notes: Q1 FY27 profit, NII, NIM, NPA, PCR and capital-adequacy figures were cross-checked across multiple financial news sources and were consistent. Valuation multiples (P/E, P/B, ROE) varied by a few points across Screener, GuruFocus and ValueResearch depending on exact date and standalone-vs-consolidated basis - a mid-range figure is used here and should be re-checked against Screener before publishing. Q2 FY27 results were not yet released at the time of writing (board meeting scheduled for 17 October 2026); nothing in this report should be mistaken for that quarter's actual numbers.
